Why beef costs more

lines.text: Why did ground beef jump about 40% since 2022?
lines.say: Why did ground beef jump about forty percent since twenty twenty-two?

lines.text: A pound went from $4.94 in August 2022 to $6.92 four years later.
lines.say: A pound went from four ninety-four in August twenty twenty-two to six ninety-two four years later.

lines.text: The reason is cows: 86.2 million in January 2026, fewest since 1951.
lines.say: The reason is cows: eighty-six point two million in January twenty twenty-six, fewest since nineteen fifty-one.

lines.text: Drought in 2022 made ranchers sell cows they couldn't feed.
lines.say: Drought in twenty twenty-two made ranchers sell cows they couldn't feed.

lines.text: Herds rebuild slowly: a heifer kept in 2025 won't be beef until about 2029.
lines.say: Herds rebuild slowly: a heifer kept in twenty twenty-five won't be beef until about twenty twenty-nine.

lines.text: In 2025, the US also paused Mexican cattle over a pest called screwworm.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, the US also paused Mexican cattle over a pest called screwworm.

lines.text: Brazilian beef faced an extra 40% tariff from August to November 2025.
lines.say: Brazilian beef faced an extra forty percent tariff from August to November twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Our math: 4 pounds a month cost about $237 a year in 2022, and $332 in 2026.
lines.say: Our math: four pounds a month cost about two hundred thirty-seven dollars a year in twenty twenty-two, and three hundred thirty-two in twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: That's about $95 more. Prices follow the herd.
lines.say: That's about ninety-five dollars more. Prices follow the herd.

post.title: Why ground beef costs 40% more than in 2022
post.ig:
Why did ground beef jump 40% since 2022? Blame the cows.
100% ground beef averaged $4.94/lb in August 2022 and $6.92 in August 2026 (BLS).
On Jan 1, 2026, the US had 86.2 million cattle, the fewest since 1951 (USDA).
Drought in 2022 forced ranchers to sell cows, and a heifer kept in 2025 doesn't produce beef until about 2029.
Imports were limited too: a 2025 screwworm pause on Mexican cattle and an extra 40% tariff on Brazilian beef from Aug to Nov 2025.
Sources: BLS average price data, USDA NASS Cattle report, NPR, UF/IFAS Extension, USDA APHIS, Beef Central.
